original_question: After a soliton scatters at a graph vertex, can the time interval on which the outgoing waves are accurately approximated by solitary waves be extended beyond the logarithmic-in-velocity scale proved in the paper? How does that longer-timescale question depend on the initial data and on the external potential?
target_in_paper: Section 2.4, unnumbered open problem immediately after Lemma 2.4: whether the post-collision validity interval for approximation by solitary outgoing waves in fast-soliton scattering on a Y-junction can be extended beyond the proved logarithmic-in-velocity scale, in light of the comparison with two-soliton scattering on the line.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the paper's open issue about extending the post-collision timescale on which the outgoing pieces remain well approximated by solitary waves. It also correctly notices that the paper compares this question with a different NLS model on the line in which longer-time behavior may depend on the initial data and an external potential.
missing_details: The paper is not about a generic graph vertex: the discussed scattering result is in Section 2.4 for the focusing cubic NLS on a three-edge star graph (a Y-junction).
The unknown is a complex-valued wavefunction on the star graph, i.e. on a Hilbert space of functions on three half-lines coupled at one vertex.

In the simplified setup used for exposition, the linear Hamiltonian is the Laplacian with Kirchhoff vertex condition; the survey notes that more general repulsive self-adjoint couplings can also be treated, but the open problem is stated after the Kirchhoff discussion.
The initial state is not arbitrary: it is a fast incoming truncated soliton placed on one edge, with large velocity v and a smooth cutoff near the vertex.
The proved post-collision approximation is specifically by one reflected and two transmitted solitary waves whose amplitudes are determined by the linear scattering matrix.

The currently proved timescale is the post-interaction interval of logarithmic order in the incoming velocity v; the refined question should state that the issue is extension beyond this O(log v) scale as v becomes large.
The paper's rigorous control in this scattering discussion is in L^2, hence chiefly for mass transmission/reflection; the draft does not specify the norm or notion of 'accurately approximated'.

The paper does not itself formulate the graph problem with an external potential. The phrase about dependence on initial data and external potential comes from an analogy with a different model, namely two-soliton scattering on the line, and should be presented as an analogue-to-be-tested rather than as an existing parameter of the graph theorem.
The quantifier should be explicit: the question concerns the high-velocity regime, i.e. for sufficiently large incoming velocity v.
To stay paper-faithful, the question should be tied to the outgoing-soliton approximation after the collision, not to pre-collision dynamics or to arbitrary long-time asymptotics on general graphs.
refined_question: In the fast-soliton scattering setting of Section 2.4 of the paper—namely, the focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on a three-edge star graph (Y-junction) with Kirchhoff vertex condition, started from a large-velocity incoming truncated soliton on one edge, for which the post-collision solution is proved in L^2 to be approximated on an O(log v) time interval by one reflected and two transmitted solitary waves with amplitudes given by the linear scattering matrix—can this post-collision validity interval be extended to longer times as v goes to infinity, and, if so, is there in the graph setting any genuine analogue of the line-problem mechanism cited in the paper in which such longer-time validity depends on the initial data and on an external potential?
justification: The draft is targeting the final open-problem paragraph of Section 2.4, not a numbered conjecture elsewhere in the paper. This survey paper does not contain a Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3 on this topic; the nearest official formulation is the unnumbered remark after Lemma 2.4. The preceding discussion in Section 2.4 fixes the relevant scope: cubic NLS, Y-junction/star graph, Kirchhoff vertex in the simplified presentation, fast incoming soliton, outgoing reflected/transmitted solitary waves, and a proved logarithmic-in-velocity post-collision timescale. The immediately following remark then explicitly asks whether the timescale of validity of approximation by the solitary outgoing waves can be extended, and says that in a different model this may depend on the initial data and external potential, but that it is unclear whether analogous considerations apply here. The refined question therefore keeps the graph problem narrow, retains the O(log v) benchmark and the outgoing-soliton approximation from the paper, and treats the 'external potential' issue only as an imported analogy from the cited line model rather than as an already-built-in feature of the graph theorem.
